training_resolution_anchoring.note: the anchoring effect now REPLICATES in all three B2 materials. Local minima at N=21 and N=33: 2.99x and 2.47x here, against 3.07x/3.17x (Mooney-Rivlin) and 4.30x/3.65x (Neo-Hookean) -- Arruda-Boyce shows the smallest effect of the three, but the same shape, at the same two resolutions, every time.
training_resolution_anchoring.conclusion: three of three B2 materials show this effect. It is a property of B2's two-resolution training protocol, not a coincidence of one or two materials. What remains unresolved (stated in the Neo-Hookean record) is whether the effect is caused by the training PROTOCOL (joint two-resolution training) or by the B2 GEOMETRY -- B1 has no equivalent two-resolution checkpoint to test against, so protocol and geometry still differ at once between every B1/B2 comparison available.
